documents.stance_why: The guidance says "The ultimate decision on whether students can use generative AI tools rests with the instructor" and sets no course-level rule of its own; its firm rules are about tools and data (only vetted tools, no Level II/III data in public tools), so the stance is delegates.

documents.stance_why: The Directive "supports the responsible use" of AI and allows it under conditions: use "only approved Generative AI", keep Level II/III data out of public tools, verify output and "disclose the use". Coder B coded restrict because of the approved-tools-only rule; the Directive does not ban AI use for its subject matter, it lets users use any vetted tool under conditions, so permit with conditions.

notes: Reconciled from coder A and coder B. Only the three included university-layer documents were coded (UDIT FAQ, UDIT Directive, CTAL course-policies page); no school or computing documents were found and courses were deferred. Recurring uncovered items kept as UNCOVERED for the next codebook review: limits on distributing AI-generated content outside the course (FAQ); aligning the course AI policy with discipline or department norms (CTAL); honor pledges as an optional measure (CTAL); students' confusion from inconsistent course AI policies (CTAL). Coder B's possible new types match these. Dropped as not a policy: coder B's CTAL unit predicting that courses requiring AI will grow (its own fit_note says it is not a requirement).
